claims.nodeLabel: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
claims.text: DIA Info Memo U-09-2660 (13 Nov 2009) frames the two names as the same thing: it evaluates 'a request from Senator Harry Reid (enclosure 1) to establish a restricted special access program (SAP) for the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Application Program Contract, referred to in Senator Reid's letter as the Advanced Aerospace Threat and Identification Program (AAITP).'

claims.nodeLabel: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
claims.text: The concealment-relevant fact is not that AATIP was fake but that it was administratively real and deliberately kept out of SAP channels. DIA's own recommendation against a SAP (Nov 2009) is what later allowed officials to characterise AATIP as low-significance: a program denied special protection leaves no SAP paper trail to point at.

claims.nodeLabel: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
claims.text: DIA Info Memo U-09-2660 (13 Nov 2009): 'All program documents delivered to [DIA] during FY 2009 (the first year of the program) were unclassified because the contractor had not established a secure facility, and program employees were being vetted for clearances. In FY 2010, most research products will remain at the unclassified level. However, four to six of the original technical reports will be expanded to include classified data.'

claims.nodeLabel: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
claims.text: The FY2010 pivot described in U-09-2660 — 'four to six of the original technical reports will be expanded to include classified data', focused on 'foreign research in a particular technology area' — is the point at which the publicly-visible DIRD series stops and the record goes dark. The 37-38 released DIRDs are, by DIA's own account, the unclassified subset.

claims.text: Memo header: 'DEFENSE INTELLIGENCE AGENCY, WASHINGTON, D.C. 20340-5100 — INFO MEMO, U-09-2660, NOV 13 2009. FOR: DIRECTOR, SPECIAL PROGRAMS, OFFICE OF THE UNDER SECRETARY OF DEFENSE FOR INTELLIGENCE. SUBJECT: (U) Review of Special Access Program Request.'

claims.nodeLabel: DIA Memorandum: Review of Special Access Program Request (U-09-2660CE-IM)
claims.text: Finding: 'In reviewing the deliverables to date and looking ahead to planned production in fiscal year (FY) 2010, DIA cannot find adequate justification to establish a restricted SAP... Based on classification levels of current and projected program deliverables, there are insufficient grounds to classify this open program, invoke alternative or compensatory control measures (ACCM), or establish a restricted SAP.'

claims.sourceText: USAF biography https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Biographies/Display/article/104776/major-general-william-n-mccasland/ compared against DIA INFO MEMO U-09-2660, https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237611/
claims.text: That Special Programs directorate is OUSD(AT&L), NOT OUSD(I). DIA's INFO MEMO U-09-2660 of 13 November 2009 declining the AAWSAP special access program request was addressed to 'DIRECTOR, SPECIAL PROGRAMS, OFFICE OF THE UNDER SECRETARY OF DEFENSE FOR INTELLIGENCE'. The two offices are distinct and McCasland held the AT&L one; nothing here places him in the AAWSAP decision.

edges.note: The request and the refusal. Reid's 24 June 2009 letter asked for a restricted SAP; DIA Info Memo U-09-2660 of 13 November 2009 is the answer - 'DIA cannot find adequate justification to establish' it. DIA Info Memo U-10-2552 then records that Deputy Secretary Lynn and the Director met Senator Reid in November 2009 to discuss it. A documented request, a documented denial, and a documented meeting between them.
